about: classify_threat's walk set (E3, the operator's order of 2026-10-28; PHASE8_PLAN 17.1 S7; 13.6). Each case is one detection of the Lab 8 walk of 2026-10-27 on the network SDN lab (22:17 to 23:34 UTC, the loop every 10 s, Ryu 4.34 over Open vSwitch 2.17.12, Mininet's hosts 192.0.2.1 to .4; s1 holds h1 on port 1, h2 on 2, the link on 3; s2 h3 on 1, h4 on 2, the link on 3), its detection as the loop kept it (the NMAS host's sdn_responses.jsonl, the response's proposed row) and the sdn section of the evidence pack the loop kept when it fired (evidence_packs.jsonl), each section checked equal to what the walk's own AI call was sent (the pack's own sdn:<n> references left out: the classifier is never sent them); `from` names the Lab 8 file and call, the response and the pack, and `edit` the one change, if any. Cases 1 to 8 are every threat detection the loop classified: the scan on both switches, the flood on both (its first run, whose L2 flows name no source address, so only a person's decision passes; its second, whose L4 flow names h2), the injected flow on s1 (rebuilt through the displaced-flow and effect code, which the walk predates) and the redirect on s2 (as kept: the effect needs s2's whole table, which the pack does not keep). Cases 9 to 20 are objective 2.3's twelve scan-fallback false positives (2.3-fallback-fp.txt, each by its call): the rule fired at 100 packets a second on L2 and L3 flows that cannot show ports; none was a scan. The expectation is read from each port's own counters: nine are the pair checks' TCP transfers (one direction 43 to 44 kB segments, the other 66-byte acks at a matching rate: a transfer and its acks), no threat; three are the walk's real flood (1,300 to 1,500 packets a second of 1,512-byte packets with about 1 a second back: one-way UDP from h2), a flood, with no action, since the fallback names no source and so no source action can pass Mercury's check. Cases 21 to 25 are the walk's quiet collections (lab8/sdn-normal-run1 to 5.json, 00:17 to 00:18 UTC on the 28th), each with the scan rule's packet-rate fallback threshold lowered so it fires on a link port's own traffic, built by the real rule and section builder: a false positive Mercury's rules made, which the classifier should call no threat. Expectations written 2026-10-28 from the evidence, before any run of this set; judged by cases.sdn_classify_misses. Not yet measured: no recording here. tests/test_sdn_classify_walk_cases.py checks every case but the two scans and the redirect is what the code builds now from the evidence it holds, and names those three and why.
